title: Knowledge check: Accessible Forms and Dynamic Interfaces

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Accessible Forms and Dynamic Interfaces”?
options: Every Vue 3 application must use TypeScript.
A type checker replaces browser and component tests.
Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
Type annotations automatically validate HTTP response objects at runtime.
questions.answer_key: Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Accessible Forms and Dynamic Interfaces directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Labeling form fields”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Ignore rejected requests if the local form looked valid.
Bind the input to a clear state value, validate before sending, and show accessible field-specific and server-side errors.
A client-side required attribute replaces server validation.
A placeholder is a complete accessible label.
questions.answer_key: Bind the input to a clear state value, validate before sending, and show accessible field-specific and server-side errors.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Labeling form fields”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Accessible Forms and Dynamic Interfaces” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
